solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Brief article largely altered in album

indicators.note: largely means most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: altered says the letters of in album are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor cuts down a feature piece and reshuffles it into a photo album.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbnail sketch or account is a short, concise one, so as an adjective the word means short or concise.

clue.text: Tramps begin cycling?

indicators.note: cycling moves the first letter of the word for begin round to the end

parts.note: begin means start

explanation.definitionFit: Tramp is an old slang insult for a promiscuous woman, as is tart, so the plurals are synonyms.

clue.text: Apprehend thug at ground where the gullible may venture?

indicators.note: ground is the past tense of grind, so these letters are crushed into a new order

explanation.surface: Police seize a thug on some patch of land that only a naive person would wander onto.
explanation.walkthrough: To lead someone up the garden path is to deceive them, so the gullible are the ones who end up there.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'lead someone up the garden path' means to mislead them, so this route is where dupes are taken.

clue.text: Happened to turn up a month before woman has done likewise

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the second
in a down clue turn up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: Feb is the short form of February

indicators.note: done likewise means the woman's name is also turned up, read backwards

parts.note: Nella is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Something happened to occur in late winter, just before a woman did the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Befallen is the past participle of befall, meaning occurred to or overtook someone, as in 'what has befallen him'.

clue.text: 50 per cent of diaries, a hit when put on screen

indicators.note: in a down clue put on means placed above, so these pieces come first

parts.note: to bat is to hit, as in cricket

indicators.note: fifty per cent means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: journals are diaries

explanation.surface: Half of someone's diary entries, plus a smack, end up shown on the big screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'put on screen' as filming; in fact 'screen' alone is the definition. The French term is used in English for a lampshade or a sloping window screen.
explanation.definitionFit: An abat-jour is a shade or slanted screen that deflects light, such as a lampshade or skylight baffle.

clue.text: Where girl may go, boy almost stops

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a lad is a boy
an engine that dies stops

explanation.surface: A boy nearly gets in the way of where a girl might be heading.
explanation.walkthrough: The ladies is the British name for a women's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The ladies is a women's lavatory, the place a girl may need to visit when out.

clue.text: Gangland boss potentially runs book when fighter boxes

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the fighter holds the other letters

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter jet
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A crime boss might run an illegal betting book on a boxing match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighter' and 'boxes' suggest a boxer, but the fighter is a jet plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Big is the slang name for the head of a criminal organisation.

clue.text: Feature parent outside hospital department

indicators.note: outside means the parent wraps around the department

parts.note: mum is a mother, a parent
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A mother waits outside a ward at the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Mentum is the anatomical term for the chin, one of the facial features.

clue.text: UN squabbled about splitting bill for cheap fare?

indicators.note: splitting means these letters go inside the bill, breaking it apart

parts.note: a bird's bill is its beak

indicators.note: about signals the letters of UN squabbled are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: United Nations delegates argue over how to divide the bill for an inexpensive meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a restaurant check, but it is a bird's beak. Bubble and squeak is a British dish of fried leftover potato and cabbage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubble and squeak is a thrifty dish made from leftover vegetables, so it is inexpensive food.

clue.text: Barge in cut transporting lost crate

indicators.note: transporting means carrying, so the cut holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a gash is a cut

indicators.note: lost means the letters of crate have gone astray into a new order

explanation.surface: A cargo of boxes goes missing from a canal barge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barge' looks like a boat in this freight story; 'Barge in' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To gatecrash is to enter a party or event uninvited, pushing in where one is not wanted.

clue.text: Liqueur recalled: first rate, rich — a tip for dinner!

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so everything after it is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first rate, with the 1 read as I
fat means rich, as in a fat profit

indicators.note: the tip here is the end letter of dinner

explanation.surface: A diner remembers an excellent rich liqueur and a gratuity left after the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like a gratuity for the meal; it is the end of the word dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratafia is an almond- or fruit-kernel-flavoured cordial, a sweet alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Idiot contributing to never-ending battle

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone foolish keeps adding fuel to an endless war.
explanation.definitionFit: Dingbat is informal slang for a stupid or eccentric person, a fool.

clue.text: Wonderful hawk circling wide

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the word for hawk surrounds the other letter

parts.note: to hawk goods is to sell them
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A splendid bird of prey wheels in broad circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' paints a bird; it is the verb for peddling goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Swell is dated informal slang, chiefly American, for excellent or great.

clue.text: Nobody in particular serving American general

parts.note: GI Joe is a serving American soldier, so Joe stands for one
public means general, as in the general public

explanation.surface: An ordinary soldier serves under a US general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' suggests an army officer next to the serving soldier, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Public is a name for the ordinary, typical member of the population, an anonymous everyman.

clue.text: Highlands dish given to the French

parts.note: a plate is a dish
aux is French for 'to the' before a plural noun

explanation.surface: A dish served up to French diners.
explanation.definitionFit: Plateaux, the French-style plural, are areas of high, level ground, so uplands.

clue.text: Pacific group turn on Paisley

indicators.note: turn means the letters of on Paisley twist around into a new order

explanation.surface: An island community starts to attack the Reverend Ian Paisley, the Northern Ireland politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Polynesia is the large group of islands in the central and southern Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Facts somewhat overturned

indicators.note: overturned means the phrase is flipped, read from end to start

parts.note: somewhat means a tad, a little

explanation.surface: Accepted truths are partly reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are pieces of information gathered for analysis, so the facts or figures known.

clue.text: Try stopping animal hater

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the word for try sits inside the animal

parts.note: a deer is an animal
to test something is to try it

explanation.surface: An attempt to block an animal by someone who loathes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A detester is one who loathes something intensely, someone full of hatred.

clue.text: Reason to include major road loop for plant

indicators.note: to include means the word for reason contains the other pieces

parts.note: wit is reason or sense, as in out of one's wits
the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, written with I for 1
a tab is a small loop of fabric for hanging something

explanation.surface: Planners have a reason to add a ring road to a major route.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the major road from London to Edinburgh. The plant is named for thorns that catch at passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: Wait-a-bit is the name of several thorny shrubs, especially African acacias, whose hooked spines snag clothing.

clue.text: Unknown party left doing U-turn in E European city

indicators.note: doing a U-turn means the string goes back the way it came, so read backwards

parts.note: Z is a mathematical unknown
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A mystery party of left-wingers performs a reversal in an Eastern European city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodz is Poland's third-largest city, an industrial centre in central Poland.

clue.text: Queen opening museum: horse gallery

indicators.note: opening means the queen gets inside, splitting the museum's name open

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
horse is slang for heroin, whose abbreviation is H

explanation.surface: The Queen opens a museum's new horse gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse gallery' reads as an exhibit; 'gallery' alone is the definition. ER is the late Queen's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A verandah is a roofed open porch along a house's side, a kind of gallery.

clue.text: Small donkey died and reeked

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
moke is British slang for a donkey
D is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A little donkey died and stank.
explanation.definitionFit: To reek originally meant to give off smoke, so smoked and reeked are synonyms.

clue.text: Object emphatically struck ledge after repeatedly losing height

indicators.note: repeatedly losing means the letter for height is removed more than once, from each word

parts.note: to hit is to strike, so struck can be hit
a shelf is a ledge
H is the abbreviation for height, here taken away twice

explanation.surface: Something hit a ledge after falling from a great height again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' suggests a thing falling; it is the grammatical object, and 'itself' is an emphatic or reflexive pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Itself is the reflexive form of it, used as an object or for emphasis, as in 'the thing itself'.

clue.text: First signs of near miss might indicate such a small distance

definitions.text: First signs of near miss might indicate such a small distance

parts.words: First signs of near miss might indicate such a small distance
parts.note: the initials of near and miss make the symbol nm, the unit abbreviation for a billionth of a metre

explanation.surface: A close shave suggests things were a tiny distance apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters N and M are the standard abbreviation of the unit, and a near miss also implies a very small gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanometre is one billionth of a metre, an extremely tiny length used for atoms and wavelengths.

clue.text: Hat not right for combined forces doing tour?

indicators.note: not means the letter for right is removed from the word

parts.note: torque is the turning effect of forces, as if forces were going round on a tour

explanation.surface: A soldier swaps his right-hand cap for one suited to allied troops on a tour of duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combined forces' and 'tour' suggest an army; torque is a twisting force in physics.
explanation.definitionFit: A toque is a small brimless hat, most familiar as a chef's tall white cap.

clue.text: City in Europe being overlooked by church

indicators.note: overlooked means left out, so the letters for church are dropped

parts.note: essence means being, one's fundamental nature
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A European city's very existence is ignored by the church.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'overlooked by' could mean placed below; here it means ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is a major industrial city in the Ruhr area of western Germany.

clue.text: Old explorer not about to drop hamper

indicators.note: to drop means these letters are removed from the end of the explorer's name

parts.note: Sir Ernest Shackleton was an Antarctic explorer

indicators.note: about means the word not is turned round

explanation.surface: An old explorer decides against losing his picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a basket, but it is the verb meaning hinder.
explanation.definitionFit: To shackle someone is to restrict or restrain them, so it is a synonym of hinder.

clue.text: Soap bars perhaps made from best tallow? Not half

indicators.note: made from says the letters are reworked into something new
not half means only the front half of tallow is used, its second half dropped

explanation.surface: Soap was once made from good-quality animal fat, only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bars of soap are sold as tablets, the term for small flat solid blocks of a substance.

clue.text: Out of a relationship, one side being hurt

indicators.note: one side here means just the right-hand half of the word is kept

parts.note: someone unattached is single, not in a relationship

explanation.surface: After a breakup, one partner is left feeling wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: UNATTACHED splits evenly into UNATT and ACHED; 'one side' keeps the right half.
explanation.definitionFit: Ached is the past tense of ache, meaning was sore or suffered pain.

clue.text: Herald in front getting keepsake

parts.note: fore means at the front
a token is a keepsake or memento

explanation.surface: A messenger at the front of a procession receives a souvenir.
explanation.definitionFit: To foretoken is to give advance warning or sign of something, to presage it.
